text:
Maya (CEO): Quick post-all-hands thread on the wins/losses segment. If you weren't there, recording is up  drop questions here.
Liam (Head of Sales): Field summary: we closed a mid-market deal after offering a short, scoped eval; lost a couple of early-stage startups that chose cheaper quantized self-hosts.
Elena (Customer Success): Confirmed. Customers that stayed cite our eval help (sanitization + scoring) as the differentiator, not raw latency numbers.
Sam P. (VP Product): For losses, was it purely price or also perceived ops burden?
Liam (Head of Sales): Primarily price + fear of ongoing spend. They preferred one-time infra lift and ops owned internally.
Rohit (Solutions Eng): Demo note: reliability wins came from pre-warming KV caches and short-lived pinned pools during pilot windows. Worked well when combined with a rollback plan.
Anya (PM): Product actions proposed: 1) public "latency profile" explainer; 2) "Starter Dedicated" quickstart for small teams; 3) standard eval-assistance add-on template.
LegalBot: Recommend add-on template with capped hours (e.g., 12 eng hours), defined deliverable, and exclusions. Legal will draft once Product/Sales propose pricing.
Elena (Customer Success): Also want an "eval checklist" Sales can use: data prep steps, PII redaction, sample prompts and success criteria.
Sam P. (VP Product): I'll own the latency explainer. Anya will draft the Starter quickstart and Sales slide. Rohit to add tokenization gotchas appendix.
Maya (CEO): Can we get drafts by next Tue? Also agree to offer a scoped, billable eval add-on to close deals but keep scope tight.
Anya (PM): Captured. Action items: latency doc, starter quickstart, eval add-on template, Sales cheat-sheet slide. Posting drafts in #docs when ready.
Liam (Head of Sales): I'll DM anonymized RFP snippets to help price the starter package.
Maya (CEO): Thanks. We'll review progress in leadership sync. Tag Anya or Sam for follow-ups. :sparkles:
